title: What Single-Molecule Transistors Is
definition: Single-Molecule Transistors: transistors made of individual molecules.

title: Real Research Today: Single-Molecule Transistors
definition: Today's documented research behind Single-Molecule Transistors.
description:

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as transistor logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Single-Molecule Transistors Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Single-Molecule Transistors: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Single-Molecule Transistors — transistors made of individual molecules.

Phase 1 — Prove (molecule bridges): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (transistor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (gate control): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (reproducibility): transistor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and labs-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
